memory_verse.label: Bible Reference
memory_verse.text: But the Lord God called to the man, "Where are you?" — Gen 3:9 (NIV)

devotion.label: Devotion
devotion.text:
Three small words, and yet how much they carry. Adam and Eve are hiding among the trees, and God calls out: "Where are you?"

We must not think God asked because He had lost them. The God who sees all things knew exactly where Adam was crouching (Ps 139:7–10). This was not a question for God's sake, but for Adam's. It was the voice of a Father seeking a child who had run away — an invitation to come out of hiding and face the truth rather than bury it deeper.

Isn't it striking? After the very first sin in human history, God's first words are not thunder and condemnation, but a searching, seeking question. The rebel does not run to God — so God comes calling for the rebel. Grace is already at work in the garden, before a single word of judgment is spoken.

And that same question still echoes to us. When we have wandered, when guilt makes us want to hide, God's voice comes gently: "Where are you?" Not to shame us, but to draw us back.

Dear friend, this seeking God has never stopped calling. He would one day come in person, in Jesus, to seek and to save the lost (Lk 19:10). You may feel far away today, tangled in your own fig leaves and trees. But listen — He is still calling your name, still inviting you to come home.

reflection.label: Reflection
reflection.text:
1. If God asked you "Where are you?" today, how would you honestly answer?
2. What keeps you hiding rather than coming out into the light before God?
3. How does it move you that God seeks you first, before you seek Him?

prayer.label: Prayer
prayer.text: Father, thank You that You come seeking me even when I hide. When I hear You gently ask "Where are you?", give me courage to step out of the shadows and come honestly to You. Thank You that in Jesus You sought and saved me. Amen.
